name: Repair from use and the standing defect backlog
summary: The first release scoped from USING the packaged application rather than from review findings alone. v0.6.0's premortem carried one line a harness cannot close — install the DMG and use it — and closing it immediately returned a layout defect that five ABORT stations, the host gates and a 40-check screen walk had all passed over. This release carries that fix and clears the standing defect backlog: every open issue that is a defect rather than a roadmap milestone. Two of those defects were created by the v0.6.0 work itself — a UI route the contextual-bar removal took away, and a harness check that cannot fail — which is the argument for closing them here rather than carrying them further.
updateSource: Scoped from use of the packaged v0.6.0 build

required.title: A settings row's control lines up with the title that names it
required.summary: Reported from real use of the packaged 0.6.0 build, against the Code Block dialog. Every .settings-row is a two-line label beside a control laid out with align-items: center, which centres the control against the whole label group rather than the title it names — measured at +9.0px. The row is top-aligned now, with the title and the control sharing one band (--row-band), so the description hangs below without pulling the control down. Central, not local: the dialog reuses .settings-row, so the same misalignment was in all 13 rows across the dialog and the Editor and Appearance settings. All now measure +0.0px. Two regressions the extended test caught before merge: the band rule out-specified .settings-toggle and STRETCHED the pill from 20px to 32px, and min-height on a content-box element grew the segmented control to 38px. A stretched pill still centres, so the offset assertion passed it — its size is asserted separately.

required.title: A panic before the App exists leaves no trail
required.summary: GitHub #62. App.reportPanic covers every bound method, but not a panic raised before the App and its event log are constructed — inside NewApp(), or on the main goroutine before startup fires. Both kill the process with nothing recorded and no dialog. Closing it means changing construction order to open a trail that does not depend on the App, not adding another guard. NOTE: the issue's stated premise is now partly stale — it describes the replaced framework's Run() and its lifecycle callbacks, which no longer exist. The window it names is real, but its shape changed with the host replacement and must be re-measured against the current startup path before the fix is designed.

required.title: A repeating panic evicts the context needed to diagnose it
required.summary: GitHub #63. The event log is bounded at 2000 entries and trim keeps the newest, which is right in general and wrong for a repeating panic: a panic in a debounced path records once per tick, so the FIRST panic and everything leading to it are evicted and 2000 copies of the last are kept. That inverts what root-cause analysis needs. The refused-link-scheme precedent in this repo solves the same shape by capping per distinct key; of the three options the issue records, recording the first N occurrences then a periodic still-happening summary preserves the most diagnostic value and is the most code.

required.title: -close-dirty cannot fail: both guard outcomes report PASS
required.summary: GitHub #100, found while re-driving the host modes for v0.6.0. reportCloseDecision prints PASS on both branches because it does not know which mode it is running in, so under -close-dirty a guard that ALLOWS the close — the exact failure the mode exists to catch, unsaved work dropped silently — is reported as a passing clean close. The guard itself is correct; this is a reporting defect. A check that passes on every outcome is indistinguishable from a check that was never run.

required.title: Code block language picker writes the display name into the fence
required.summary: GitHub #78. The vendored node view's picker, adopted in #77 when the app stopped drawing its own chrome, sets the block language from LanguageDescription.name — the DISPLAY name — so a file gains a capitalised fence where every other route in the app writes the normalized lowercase id. Nothing renders differently and no content is lost, but this project holds a byte-identical round-trip corpus and a 49-construct fidelity survey, so an inconsistency that depends on which control the user reached for matters more here. Already asserted in e2e so it cannot change unnoticed in either direction. Normalizing on serialize is NOT the fix: it would rewrite user-authored capitalised fences, which the fidelity survey would correctly fail.

required.title: Image Reveal in Finder has no route in the UI
required.summary: GitHub #85, created by the v0.6.0 contextual-bar removal. Every other control in the bar's image group was duplication of what the editor already provides; Reveal was not, because it is a desktop capability that calls through to the host and no editor plugin can provide it. The capability is intact behind the API and still works when invoked; what it no longer has is anything to click. The awkwardness is that the image block is entirely vendored, unlike the mermaid preview the Diagram assistant was relocated onto, so appending to its operation group means injecting into DOM the node view owns and rebuilds. The app now builds its own menu bar, which is a route the bar-era options did not have.

required.title: Tab indents by the same amount in every mode
required.summary: Reported from real use. Measured on one document: Tab inserted 4 spaces in raw and 2 in the formatted view's code blocks. Neither was wrong alone — raw used the app's own constant, and the formatted view is CodeMirror, whose indentUnit facet defaults to two — but nothing connected them, so the same keystroke on the same document produced different text depending on the mode, which split view makes routine. Both now read frontend/dist/src/indent.js. tools/vendor.sh exports CodeMirror's facet so the decision lives in app code rather than in a shell script that rewrites a vendored artifact, and it DISCOVERS the minified name from the facet's own definition rather than hardcoding it, because the name is chosen by the minifier and the definition is not.

required.title: The diagram assistant's preview and fields stay inside their boxes
required.summary: Reported from real use. Two defects in one dialog, both measured. The field inputs had width:100% plus 9px padding and a 1px border on a content-box element, so a 240px column held a 260px input that ran underneath the preview beside it. Separately the preview's SVG was bounded in width but not height, and place-items: center on an item taller than its box overflows BOTH ways — the diagram sat 9px out of the top and 9px out of the bottom, and the clipped top could not be scrolled to. Fixed with box-sizing on the input, max-height on the SVG, and `safe` centring so an item that does not fit falls back to start alignment instead of being centred out of view. This is the second content-box overflow found this release; see the note on adopting a global border-box.

outOfScope.title: The five open roadmap milestones
outOfScope.reason: #5, #10, #11, #12 and #13 are open, but they are multi-release trackers — post-alpha remediation, direct export, comments and review, share/sync and extensions architecture, packaging and signing — not defects. Excluded because each is a milestone in its own right, not because they are unimportant.

blockers.title: The WYSIWYG surface still re-serializes the whole document
blockers.summary: Carried forward unchanged from v0.6.0. The editor parses to ProseMirror's model and re-serializes everything, so a construct nobody surveyed is still respelled. Only source-preserving editing would close the class. This is recorded here because the version number moves to 1.x, which reads as a maturity claim this blocker contradicts; the version was chosen by the maintainer with that stated.
